candidates.exact_span: The following pollutants may not be introduced into the treatment facility:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether these pretreatment prohibitions govern only indirect dischargers into the POTW or also frame enforceable limits and obligations for the permittee's own evaluated discharge points changes which parameters and requirements enter A/B scope.

candidates.exact_span: wastestreams with a closed cup flashpoint of less than 140 degrees Fahrenheit or 60 degrees Centigrade using the test methods specified in 40 CPR 261.21
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric flashpoint threshold and specified test method; different readings of applicability or method choice change whether a reported measurement triggers a limit comparison.

candidates.exact_span: discharges with pH lower than 5.0, unless the works are specifically designed to accommodate such discharges
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a numeric pH floor with a design-accommodation exception; whether the exception applies or is documented changes enforceable limit selection (A) and how missing or conditional evidence is classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: Solid or viscous pollutants in amounts which will cause obstruction to the flow in the POTW, resulting in Interference,·
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a qualitative interference standard without a fixed numeric limit; interpretation determines whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable versus report-only or non-numeric evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: Any pollutant, including oxygen demanding pollutants (e.g., BOD), released in a discharge at a flow rate and/or pollutant concentration which will cause Interference with the POTW,·
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links parameters such as BOD to an interference standard rather than a stated numeric limit; different readings of enforceability change whether reported BOD/flow data receive numeric limit comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Heat in amounts which will inhibit biological activity in the POTW resulting in Interference but in no case heat in such quantities that the temperature at the POTW treatment plant exceeds 40 degrees Centigrade (104 degrees Fahrenheit) unless the Approval Authority, upon request of the POTW, approves alternate temperature limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: Combines qualitative interference language with a numeric 40 °C cap and an approval-based alternate-limit exception; interpretation of which branch governs and whether alternate limits were approved changes applicable limit and unresolved missing-evidence handling.

candidates.exact_span: Petroleum oil, non-biodegradable cutting oil, or products of mineral oil origin in amounts that will cause interference or pass through
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a qualitative pass-through/interference standard for oil-related parameters without fixed numeric limits, affecting whether measurements are compared to numeric limits or treated as non-numeric obligations.

candidates.exact_span: Any trucked or hauled pollutants, except at discharge points designated by the POTW.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prohibits hauled pollutant introductions except at designated points; whether a discharge point is POTW-designated changes which limits and monitoring obligations attach to that point.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall require any indirect discharger to the treatment works to comply with the reporting requirements of Sections 204(b), 307, and 308 of the Act, including any requirements established under 40 CPR Part 403.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a permittee obligation to impose federal pretreatment reporting requirements on indirect dischargers; interpretation of which Part 403 reporting applies changes evaluated monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall provide adequate notice of the following:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a notice obligation whose triggers are defined in the following bullets; whether notice was required in FY2025 depends on interpreting those conditions.

candidates.exact_span: Any new introduction of pollutants into the treatment works from an indirect discharger which would be subject to Sections 301 and 306 of the Act If it were directly discharging those pollutants,·
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines a conditional notice trigger tied to indirect-discharge character and CWA section applicability; different readings of 'new introduction' or direct-discharge equivalency change whether notice monitoring was required and how absent notice is classified.

candidates.exact_span: Any substantial change in the volume or character of pollutants being introduced into the treatment works by a source introducing pollutants into the treatment works at the time of issuance of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a notice trigger based on substantial changes from baseline sources; interpreting 'substantial change' or baseline scope changes whether notice was required and whether missing documentation reflects conditional non-requirement or unresolved obligation.
